Caught mid-pour, tipping a dark vial over a goblet, her eyes flicking sideways — checking she's alone — a slow private smile spreading before the last drop falls.
Lips pressed to a cracked pendant, eyes squeezed shut, whispering something with fierce quiet urgency, knuckles pale around the chain, caught before she knew anyone was watching.
Fingertip raised to her mouth, drawing the bead of blood slowly across her lower lip, gaze distant, expression neither pained nor troubled — only deeply, privately satisfied.
Veil half-lifted, chin tilted, catching her own reflection in dark glass, studying the stranger there with cold fascination, one finger tracing the mirror's edge like a question.
Letter crumpled in both fists, eyes closed, jaw tight, a single tear tracking her cheek while her expression hardens into something far more dangerous than grief.
Candle flame inches from her lips, breath held, watching the smoke curl before she blows — slow, deliberate, like extinguishing something that was never meant to survive the night.
Collar clasp undone at the throat, head tilted back, breathing slowly in the dark corridor, caught between relief and recklessness, expression raw and unguarded.
Palm flat on the table, studying every line of her own hand with clinical intensity, whispering numbers or names quietly, lips barely moving, oblivious to being seen.
Kneeling beside a low flame, pouring dark powder in a careful circle, lips moving in silence, expression focused and devout, hair falling forward to hide her face.
Smiling in the deep shadow beside a doorframe — not at anyone, at something internal — the smile slow and crooked and entirely without warmth, caught a half-second too long.
Goblet raised but not yet drunk, held at chin level, eyes closed, inhaling through her nose first — as if confirming something — expression suspended between decision and commitment.
Caught pulling a folded page from inside her sleeve, glancing over one shoulder, thumb pressed to the wax seal, hesitating with everything visible in her face.
Kneeling at a low mirror, veil pooled behind her, touching her own jaw with two fingers as if checking for something invisible, expression uncertain and quietly afraid.
Standing in the corridor dark, pressing a sealed letter against the wall with her palm flat, forehead bowed almost to it, breathing heavily like a confession she can't speak.
Caught mid-whisper over someone's sleeping form, lips brushing the air just above their cheek, eyes open and cold, expression somewhere between tenderness and deliberate ruin.
Back turned, unfastening the long row of clasps along her cuff, each one slow, methodical, watched only by the mirror reflecting a face she hasn't arranged for anyone.
Tipping a small vial into her own palm, tilting it under candlelight, weighing it, tilting again — then closing her fist around it before anyone else can see.
Caught tracing a symbol onto fogged glass with one fingertip, expression blank and dreaming, breath still misting the surface, the mark almost finished before she notices she's watched.
Wiping her mouth with the back of her wrist, eyes forward and hard, a goblet set aside, expression composed already — whatever feeling crossed it is gone, locked down.
Crouched beside a low shelf, reading a label with her face inches away, lips moving slightly, then carefully — deliberately — reversing two bottles before standing and smoothing her skirt.
Caught mid-tear on a letter, pulling it cleanly down the center, expression flat, eyes dry, methodical as if destroying evidence rather than something that once meant everything.
One hand gripping the banister, leaning into shadow to watch someone below, chin low, breathing controlled, unsmiling — caught in the act of memorizing something she was never meant to see.
Pressing her wrist to her lips briefly, not a bite, not a kiss — something in between, private and habitual, caught mid-ritual before she lowers her arm and looks up.
Caught swallowing something with no water, throat moving, eyes closed for three seconds exactly, then open again — expression returned to neutral, as if nothing passed between her lips at all.
Kneeling at the hearthstone, feeding a ribbon of paper into the flame slowly, watching each word blacken and curl, expression serene, almost reverent, finished before the last word is gone.
Caught mid-tilt, pouring something dark from a vial into her goblet, lips parted slightly, eyes flicking sideways as if she heard footsteps she wasn't expecting just yet.
Fingers pressed flat against the mirror, studying her own reflection with cold fascination, like she's negotiating with whoever stares back rather than recognizing herself.
Letter crumpled half-open in her fist, jaw tight, one tear sliding unchecked while her other hand closes around a pendant she hasn't released in minutes.
Leaning into the candle flame almost too close, whispering something to it before exhaling — cheeks hollow, eyes fixed, the whole room tilting toward whatever she just asked of it.
Caught lifting the hem of her veil with two fingers, not to reveal herself but to peer through it at something across the room no one else seems to notice.
